title: B+-Tree Index
overview:
In this project you will implement a **disk-based B+-Tree index** for integer keys.

A B+-Tree is a balanced search tree optimized for disk-based storage systems. Unlike in-memory binary search trees, B+-Trees have a high branching factor (hundreds of keys per node) to minimize the number of disk I/O operations needed for a lookup. All actual data pointers reside in leaf nodes, which are linked together via sibling pointers to support efficient range scans.

Your B+-Tree will use the Buffer Manager from Project #1 for page access. Each tree node is stored in a single page. When a node overflows (too many keys), it must be **split**, and a key is pushed up to the parent. This may cascade up to the root, potentially increasing the tree's height.

**Scope limitations:** INTEGER keys only, no delete operation, no duplicate key support (inserting an existing key updates the value).

tasks.title: Search
tasks.description: Navigate from the root to the correct leaf node to find a key.

functions.name: Search(int32_t key) → optional<page_id_t>
functions.description: Starting at `root_page_id_`, traverse the tree to find the leaf node that would contain `key`. At each internal node, use binary search (via `upper_bound`) on the keys to find the correct child pointer. At the leaf, use binary search to check for an exact match. Return the associated value if found, `nullopt` otherwise.
hints: Use `LoadNode(page_id)` to read a node from disk (provided helper).
For internal nodes: `upper_bound` returns the index of the first key > given key. The child at that index is the correct subtree.
For leaf nodes: `lower_bound` finds the position where key would be. Check `*it == key`.
This is an iterative traversal (loop until `is_leaf == true`).

functions.name: Delete(int32_t key) → bool
functions.description: Remove a key and its value from the tree. Return `false` if the key is not there.
hints: Walk to the leaf that would hold the key, the same way `Search` does.
Binary search the leaf; not found means `false`.
Erase the key and its value together, then save the leaf.
No merge or redistribute — a leaf is allowed to underflow.

tasks.title: Insert
tasks.description: Insert a key-value pair, splitting nodes as needed to maintain the B+-Tree invariants.

functions.name: Insert(int32_t key, page_id_t value)
functions.description:
Navigate to the correct leaf (like Search), tracking the path from root to leaf as a stack of `(page_id, child_index)` pairs. Insert the key/value in sorted order.

**If the leaf does not overflow** (keys.size() <= MaxKeys()), save it and return.

**If the leaf overflows**, split it in memory:
1. Create a new leaf with the upper half of keys/values.
2. Update sibling pointers (`next_leaf`).
3. Save both halves to disk.
4. Push the first key of the new leaf up to the parent via `InsertIntoInternal()`.

**Critical:** Do NOT serialize the overflowed node to disk before splitting — it exceeds DB_PAGE_SIZE and will corrupt data.
hints: Track the path: `vector<pair<page_id_t, int>> path`.
For duplicate keys: update the value and return early.
Split point: `mid = keys.size() / 2`.
Use `AllocateNode()` (provided) to create the new leaf page.
If the path is empty when a split occurs, the leaf was the root — create a new root.

functions.name: InsertIntoInternal(page_id_t node_id, int32_t key, page_id_t right_child, vector<pair<page_id_t,int>>& path)
functions.description: Insert a key and right child pointer into an internal node (called when a child node was split). If the internal node also overflows, split it: the middle key goes up to the parent, the left half stays, the right half goes to a new node. This may cascade up to the root.
hints: Use `upper_bound` to find insertion position for the key.
Insert key at position, insert right_child at position+1 in children.
Split point: `mid = keys.size() / 2`. The key at `mid` goes up (not stored in either child).
Pop from `path` to get the parent. If path is empty, create a new root.

tasks.title: Range Scan
tasks.description: Scan leaf nodes to return all entries in a key range.

functions.name: RangeScan(int32_t begin_key, int32_t end_key) → vector<pair<int32_t, page_id_t>>
functions.description: Find the leaf containing `begin_key` (traverse like Search). Then scan forward through the leaf chain using `next_leaf` sibling pointers, collecting all `(key, value)` pairs where `begin_key <= key <= end_key`. Stop when `key > end_key` or you reach the end of the chain (`next_leaf == INVALID_PAGE_ID`).
hints: Reuse the Search traversal logic to find the starting leaf.
Inner loop: iterate through keys in the current leaf.
Outer loop: follow `next_leaf` to the next leaf page.

breakdown.covers: Empty tree, single key, non-existent key
In-order, reverse, duplicate update, leaf split, multi-leaf growth, random order
Full range, partial, empty, single key, across leaves
Single key, non-existent, empty tree, other keys preserved, delete then re-insert
Insert/search/delete sweep, random order, delete-all then reinsert, interleaved ops, range scan after delete

testing.note: Project #1-#2 reference implementations are provided. The buffer pool size is set to 64 frames for tree tests.
testing.platforms: macOS or Linux, on either Intel or ARM. On Windows, build inside WSL: a native Windows toolchain is refused, because the reference libraries these downloads carry are built for macOS and Linux only.

hints: Start with Search — it's the simplest and helps you verify that LoadNode/SaveNode work correctly.
Implement Insert without splits first. Insert up to MaxKeys() entries and verify Search finds them all.
Then add leaf splitting. Test with sequential inserts that exceed one leaf's capacity.
InsertIntoInternal is the trickiest part. The middle key goes UP (removed from the node), unlike leaf splits where the split key stays in the right leaf.
Use small test cases you can trace by hand. Draw the tree after each insertion.
The provided `SerializeNode`/`DeserializeNode` handle all disk formatting — you only work with `BPTreeNode` structs in memory.
Node capacity: with DB_PAGE_SIZE=4096, each leaf holds ~510 keys. You need >510 inserts to trigger the first split.

submission.where: Upload the archive to PLMS (https://plms.postech.ac.kr) under Project #3 before the deadline. Submissions sent by email, or left anywhere else, are not collected.
submission.note: Keep the original directory layout inside the archive (src/…), so the files drop straight back into the project tree. Submit only the files you edited: no build/ directory, no compiled objects, no reference libraries.

blocks.text: **For each module below, write one expression that is always true of it** — true before any of its functions is called, and true again every time one of them returns. It may go false in the middle of a function; that is what makes it worth writing down.
The expression is symbols, not words:
If something is hard to put in symbols, define it as a variable in words, then use the variable in the expression:

code: P = the spaces with a car in them
F = the spaces that are empty
for i in 0 .. total_spaces-1:  i in P or i in F

blocks.text: A module holds several such expressions true at once. Pick one and get it right; you do not have to find them all.
**For each function you wrote, show your expression is still true when it returns.** A line or two each, grouped by module.
If a function cannot affect the expression, say so in one line. If it could, say which step keeps it true.
